arxiv-2104-06668.title: Field induced hysteretic structural phase switching and possible CDW in Re-doped MoTe 2
arxiv-2104-06668.creator: Aastha Vasdev 1, Suman Kamboj 1, Anshu Sirohi 1 , Manasi Mandal 2 , Sourav Marik 2 , Ravi Prakash Singh 2, Goutam Sheet 1
arxiv-2104-06668.description: Abstract Abstract Novel electronic systems displaying exotic physical properties can be derived from complex topological materials through chemical doping. MoTe 2 , the candidate type-II Weyl semimetal shows dramatically enhanced superconductivity up to 4.1 K upon Re doping in Mo sites.

arxiv-2105-00308.title: Enhanced electrical transport through wrinkles in turbostratic graphene films
arxiv-2105-00308.creator: Monika Moun 1 , Aastha Vasdev 1 , Rajashekhar Pujar 2 , K. Priya Madhuri 3 , U. Mogera 2 , Neena S. John 3, G.U. Kulkarni 2, Goutam Sheet 1
arxiv-2105-00308.description: Abstract Formation of wrinkles is a common phenomenon in the large area growth of two dimensional layered materials on metallic substrates. Wrinkles can significantly affect the working of 2D materials based large scale electronic devices and therefore, it is of utmost importance to investigate local electrical properties of such wrinkled/folded structures on 2D materials.

arxiv-2205-12564.title: Spotlights: Probing Shapes from Spherical Viewpoints
arxiv-2205-12564.creator: Jiaxin Wei, Lige Liu, Ran Cheng, Wenqing Jiang, Minghao Xu, Xinyu Jiang, Tao Sun, Sören Schwertfeger, Laurent Kneip
arxiv-2205-12564.description: Abstract Recent years have witnessed the surge of learned representations that directly build upon point clouds. Inspired by spherical multi-view scanners, we propose a novel sampling model called Spotlights to represent a 3D shape as a compact 1D array of depth values.

arxiv-2206-05615.title: Machine learning approaches for COVID-19 detection from chest X-ray imaging: A Systematic Review Corresponding author: Reinel Tabares-Soto. Email address: rtabares@autonoma.edu.co
arxiv-2206-05615.creator: Harold Brayan Arteaga-Arteaga, Melissa delaPava, Alejandro Mora-Rubio, Mario Alejandro Bravo-Ortíz, Jesus Alejandro Alzate-Grisales, Daniel Arias-Garzón, Luis Humberto López-Murillo, Felipe Buitrago-Carmona, Juan Pablo Villa-Pulgarín, Esteban Mercado-Ruiz, Simon Orozco-Arias, M. Hassaballah, Maria d
arxiv-2206-05615.description: Abstract There is a necessity to develop affordable, and reliable diagnostic tools, which allow containing the COVID-19 spreading. Machine Learning (ML) algorithms have been proposed to design support decision-making systems to assess chest X-ray images, which have proven to be useful to detect and evaluate disease progression.

arxiv-2305-09925.title: A Scalable Method for Readable Tree Layouts
arxiv-2305-09925.creator: Kathryn Gray, Mingwei Li, Reyan Ahmed, Md. Khaledur Rahman, Ariful Azad, Stephen Kobourov, Katy Börner
arxiv-2305-09925.description: Abstract Large tree structures are ubiquitous and real-world relational datasets often have information associated with nodes (e.g., labels or other attributes) and edges (e.g., weights or distances) that need to be communicated to the viewers. Yet, scalable, easy to read tree layouts are difficult to achieve.

arxiv-2504-02660.title: Complex Langevin Simulations of Supersymmetric Theories
arxiv-2504-02660.creator: ANOSH JOSEPH, ARPITH KUMAR
arxiv-2504-02660.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by ANOSH JOSEPH, ARPITH KUMAR. This review explores the Complex Langevin Method (CLM), a stochastic quantization technique designed to address the sign problem in quantum field theories with complex actions. Beginning with foundational principles, the review examines the applications of CLM across a range of models, including zero- and two-dimensional systems, supersymmetric quantum mechanics, and the IKKT matrix model, a candidate for non-perturbative string theory.

arxiv-2505-21635.title: Object Concepts Emerge from Motion
arxiv-2505-21635.creator: Haoqian Liang, Xiaohui Wang, Zhichao Li, Ya Yang, Naiyan Wang
arxiv-2505-21635.description: Abstract Object concepts play a foundational role in human visual cognition, enabling perception, memory, and interaction in the physical world. Inspired by findings in developmental neuroscience—where infants are shown to acquire object understanding through observation of motion—we propose a biologically inspired framework for learning object-centric visual representations in an unsupervised manner.

pmc-11450982.title: Utilising primary care electronic health records to deliver the ALABAMA randomised controlled trial of penicillin allergy assessment
pmc-11450982.creator: Shadia Ahmed, Joanne Fielding, Catherine E. Porter, Kelsey F. Armitage, Marta Wanat, Chris Bates, Lazarina Engonidou, Robert M. West, Ly-Mee Yu, Ushma Galal, Philip Howard, Christopher C. Butler, Sinisa Savic, Jenny Boards, Sarah Tonkin-Crine, John Parry, Sue A. Pavitt, Jonathan T. Sandoe
pmc-11450982.description: BackgroundUse of electronic health records (EHR) to provide real-world data for research is established, but using EHR to deliver randomised controlled trials (RCTs) more efficiently is less developed. The Allergy AntiBiotics And Microbial resistAnce (ALABAMA) RCT evaluated a penicillin allergy assessment pathway versus usual clinical care in a UK primary care setting.

pmc-11749893.title: Worsening preoperative functional status increases morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting: A propensity matched study of the ACS-NSQIP database
pmc-11749893.creator: Renxi Li, SeungEun Lee, William Rienas, Qianyun Luo, Daniel Rinewalt
pmc-11749893.description: IntroductionDependent functional status is correlated with increased mortality in patient undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, patients who are partially dependent and totally dependent may have different peri‑operative outcome profiles. This study aims to retrospectively examine the effect of different levels of functional dependency on post-CABG morbidity and mortality.

pmc-12561533.title: The Influence of Servant Leadership on the Professional Well-Being of Kindergarten Teachers: A Moderated Mediation Model
pmc-12561533.creator: Dongqing Yu, Wenxin Yue, Shuang Hao, Dengyin Li, Qiurong Wu, Stacey Neuharth-Pritchett
pmc-12561533.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study examined the relationships among principals’ servant leadership, kindergarten teachers’ professional well-being, psychological empowerment, and an inclusive atmosphere. A questionnaire survey was conducted with 531 kindergarten teachers using purposive sampling. Results showed that (1) principals’ servant leadership positively predicted teachers’ professional well-being; (2) servant leadership positively predicted teachers’ psychological empowerment; (3) psychological empowerment mediated the relationship between servant leadership and teachers’ professional well-being; and (4) an inclusive kindergarten climate moderated the relationship between servant leadership and psychological empowerment.

pmc-12626960.title: The shift of expenditure of medical service for diagnosis and treatment of colorectal cancer from 2005 to 2014: a hospital-based retrospective survey in Guangxi
pmc-12626960.creator: Wenjie Liang, Haiyan Lu, Kaiyong Huang, Li Yang
pmc-12626960.description: PurposeMedical expenditures for colorectal cancer (CRC) in China have risen substantially, with significant geographic disparities. This study aimed to comprehensively assess the level, temporal trends, and influencing factors of medical expenditures per patient, per clinical visit, and per day among CRC patients in Guangxi from 2005 to 2014.

pmc-12818493.title: Effects of Aircraft Noise on Pilots’ Auditory Perception
pmc-12818493.creator: LingLing Song, MengMeng Liu, ShunShun Li, YinZi Piao
pmc-12818493.description: Objective:This study aimed to investigate the effects of aircraft noise on pilots’ auditory perception and develop evidence-based control strategies.Methods:A cross-sectional study was conducted between March 2021 and May 2024. Participants were divided into two main groups: a pilot group (n = 92) and a control group of 67 healthy individuals without occupational noise exposure.
